summary.short: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (HB 1709, bill text): duties for developers, distributors and deployers of high-risk AI systems used in consequential decisions; prohibited AI uses; consumer disclosures; attorney general enforcement with civil penalties. Takes effect September 1, 2025.
summary.long: HB 1709 would add Chapter 551 to the Business & Commerce Code for non-small businesses operating in or serving Texas and for developers, distributors and deployers of high-risk AI systems. High-risk systems are substantial factors in consequential decisions, such as employment, education, financial, housing, insurance, health-care or criminal-case decisions. Developers must use reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination and give deployers a High-Risk Report; developers and distributors must correct or withdraw non-compliant systems. Deployers must use reasonable care, maintain a risk management policy, complete annual and post-modification impact assessments, and notify authorities and affected consumers of discrimination. Consumers must be told when they interact with such a system and may appeal certain consequential decisions. It bans AI uses for manipulation, social scoring, certain biometric identification, sensitive-attribute inference and unlawful deepfakes. It creates a sandbox program of up to 36 months, an Artificial Intelligence Council and an AI workforce grant program. The attorney general enforces the chapter after a 30-day cure notice, with fines of $50,000 to $100,000 per uncured violation and $80,000 to $200,000 for prohibited uses. The Act takes effect September 1, 2025.

Section 4 amends several subsections partly through bracketed deletions and renumbering (e.g. '([5]6)'); the extracted text does not mark strike-throughs, so the amendments are read from the bracket markers. Sec. 551.001(14)(C) lists items (xviii) then (xviv), an irregular numbering that likely means (xix). Sec. 551.011(b) places the cessation duty on the deployer but is triggered by a developer's discovery. Section 9 refers to 'Section 551.041', which this Act does not contain; the online mechanism is in Sec. 551.103. Sec. 551.104(a) cites 'Section 15.10' without naming its code. The text is the introduced version (status pending) and effective date is set by Section 10.
